q: Close-hauled as shown, 90 M from port, you hit a floating container. A crack in the bow takes water at every wave. What do you do first?
answer: Tack, so she heels to port and lifts the crack clear
why: On port tack she heels to starboard and buries the damage; on starboard tack it lifts clear, to be dried and patched from inside.

q: You heave to in your 20 m sloop to wait for daylight, but she forereaches at 3 kn and lies almost beam-on. What do you do?
answer: Ease the main further and lash the helm harder to leeward
why: Forereaching means the main is driving: ease it and add lee helm, so she lies 50° off the wind and drifts, leaving a slick to windward.
